chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from al-Fadl ibn Zakariyya, from Najm ibn Huthaym, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) who said:

If people knew what is in the Mosque of Kufa, they would prepare provisions and mounts for it from a distant place. Indeed, one obligatory prayer in it equals one Hajj, and one voluntary prayer in it equals one Umrah.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of praying in the Mosque of Kufa according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) highlights the immense virtue of the Mosque of Kufa, stating that its spiritual reward is so great that people would travel from far away to pray there. Specifically, a single obligatory prayer in this mosque is equivalent to the reward of one Hajj, and a single voluntary prayer is equivalent to one Umrah. This narration underscores the unique status of Kufa as a spiritual center linked to Imam Ali, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of places associated with the Ahl al-Bayt and the concept of 'fadl al-makan' (virtue of place) in devotional practice.
